hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: payment-svc-2 failed its liveness probe and restarted at 20:01:34 (#855), dropping capacity to 3/4. Payment-svc was healthy before this (GC pauses normal, all /charge calls ok in the 19:50-20:01 window). Within seconds order-service began getting 503s from payment-svc and retrying with zero delay (#872 'delay 0ms'). By 20:02:57 the client log says 'retrying immediately (attempt 3/4, backoff disabled)' (#919), so retries hammered the remaining instances. Payment-svc then reported inbound load at 3.2x baseline with 843 in flight (#938) and admission control rejecting work (#1008). Order-service exhausted retries and the gateway returned 503 after long waits (#924). The gateway 503s, load-shed messages, and metrics-agent queue drops are downstream symptoms and are not cited as cause. The small capacity loss was amplified by the zero-backoff retry policy, which fits cascading_failure. The reason the liveness probe failed is not visible in the logs. Confidence is moderate because a resource problem inside payment-svc-2 could also explain the failed probe.

Alternative: payment-svc-2 itself ran out of a resource (threads, connections) and the liveness restart is the origin. The GC lines before the restart show normal heap (about 35%), so there is no sign of memory exhaustion. Only the restart line directly supports this reading.

verdict.recommendedAction: Re-enable exponential backoff with jitter and a bounded retry count in order-service's PaymentClient (the 'backoff disabled' setting), so retries stop amplifying load on payment-svc. Restore payment-svc-2 and confirm the 4 payment-svc instances are healthy. Throttle order-service traffic to payment-svc while in-flight requests drain. Then find out why payment-svc-2 failed its liveness probe, and confirm the checkout 503 rate recovers.
